text: As the train neared Yellow Sky, Jack Potter grew more and more uneasy, for he had married without consulting the town of which he was the marshal. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a man known, liked, and feared in his corner of the West, and to marry secretly seemed to him an extraordinary crime against the town. <break time="0.8s" /> He knew full well that his marriage was an important thing to his town, an event which only the burning of the new hotel could exceed. <break time="0.8s" /> He had often thought of sending them a telegram, but a new cowardice had come upon him, and now he dreaded the moment of arrival. <break time="0.8s" /> He planned to hurry with her from the station to his house and to stay away from the citizens until their excitement had worn off a little. <break time="0.8s" /> What is worrying you, Jack, she asked, and he laughed and answered that he was only thinking of Yellow Sky, and she flushed in comprehension. <break time="0.8s" /> A sense of mutual guilt invaded their minds and developed a finer tenderness, and they looked at each other with eyes softly aglow. <break time="0.8s" /> When the train stopped at Yellow Sky, Potter gripped his wifes arm firmly to his side, and they hurried away together before the station agent could reach them.
